analysis.title: Taiwan: Sharp Rebound in Tech Production and Pullback in Consumption in October
key_insights: Taiwan October industrial production rose 5.0% mom sa, accelerating from 0.6% in September, and came in well above GS's own above-consensus forecast.
Year-on-year IP growth was 29.8% versus Bloomberg consensus 22.2%, GS forecast 24.0% and prior month 19.4%.
Tech production rebounded 8.9% mom sa after two months of contraction of roughly 0.7% to 0.8%.
Output of computers, electronic and optical products surged 43.0%, linked to AI server demand.
Electronic components output including CPUs rose a modest but steady 0.9%.
Basic metals output rose 3.9%, while chemicals, autos and machinery output fell.
Consumption pulled back: retail sales fell 1.5% mom sa after two months of expansion, led by durable goods such as electronics and passenger vehicles.
Food and beverage services sales fell 0.3% after the lunar holiday period and wholesale trade dropped 1.2%.
GS Asia MAP score is +16 with relevance 4 of 5 and a +4 surprise score versus consensus, signaling a large upside surprise.

sector_views.rationale: Computers, electronic and optical output jumped 43.0% on AI server demand, driving the strong IP beat.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Sharp acceleration from +0.6% in September, driven by AI-linked tech output.
Well above Bloomberg consensus and GS forecast, supports strong Taiwan export and tech cycle.
Actual print beat consensus by about 7.6pp.
Even GS's above-consensus forecast was exceeded.
Rebound after two months of small contractions.
Domestic consumption is lagging the tech-driven production strength.
Accelerated decline adds to the soft domestic demand picture.

risk_factors: Growth is concentrated in AI-server related output while consumption and other major industrial sectors (chemicals, autos, machinery) weaken.
Monthly tech output is volatile, with two prior months of contraction before the October rebound.
cross_bank_references: Bloomberg consensus IP growth +22.2% yoy versus GS 24.0% yoy and actual 29.8%
